concreteMissingBinding: No implemented host-owned descriptor binds the exported raw event bytes to the same selected shell tool call/process receipt, fresh event-path baseline, source/setup/tool/effective-target context and complete before/after observations before agent control resumes. Scorer rawEventsSha256/eventsComplete/setupComplete assertions alone cannot supply this join.
decision: Existing host capture/isolation can support a narrow same-tool-call export join, but no currently reviewed descriptor implements that association. Actual source-origin oracle evaluation must remain failclosed until a prospective join is implemented/reviewed/frozen; source expectation derivation and synthetic lifecycle controls may proceed independently.
establishedSourceChain: Hereby test aliases test:tsc; runTests invokes source-owned gotestsum with full ./... from tsc. Filter/options/environment are source-visible and must match expected selection.

Source-owned createCachedTool builds gotestsum by go install in tools if its tool/source-module digest cache is not already valid; a future attempt must witness allowed fresh tool/setup provenance, not admit an arbitrary supplied binary.

Inherited GOTESTSUM_JSONFILE survives Hereby run environment merging. Gotestsum uses its jsonfile option, os.Create, Go process stdout/stderr scan and writes each original event bytes plus newline. Console hide-empty/skipped-summary flags do not remove raw event records.

Existing host shell records exact docker argv/command/exit/error/stdout/stderr under timeout/output budget; historical qualifier separately copies JSONFILE after the task and source check. That establishes copied bytes and sequence, not the missing same-tool-call file/export association.
minimalProspectiveJoin: Extend the existing host-owned shell tool operation rather than create a new execution platform. Witness a fresh fixed event path baseline and retained source/tool/context/setup identities before the chosen command; preserve the exact chosen command/process receipt and session/tool-call/container identity.

After process completion, still inside that host-owned tool operation and before returning control to the agent, boundedly stat/read/export the regular event file to host-owned raw bytes; bind path, bytes/hash, export action receipt, time/order, timeout/cap/truncation/error/exit states and before/after source/tool/context checks. Missing/partial/capped/failed export remains unresolved.

Use inspected source-owned gotestsum plus the actual process/setup chain as the bounded writer association. Do not require cryptographic protection against active same-UID/adversarial upstream programs; that is outside the current operator-consistency goal. File writability by its normal producer alone is not a reason to reject practical association.

Keep tool permissions independent of hidden command/gold/scorer. Capture a configured public instrumentation path under frozen rules; allow chosen commands normally. Only the post-run scorer compares chosen command/full scope/effective context and joined event evidence with the frozen task expectation.
Freeze/review the concrete join and explicit capture limits before applicable execution. This assessment supplies no new descriptor/schema implementation, runner code or authorization.

A future raw event export must retain bytes or strict UTF8 validity before hashing, not claim lossless bytes from replacement-decoded strings.

No resource increase proposed.
unknowns: Full5972top+dynamic/raw output actual size and sufficient event cap are unknown. A bounded cap can produce honest noncompletion; no assumption that current tool-output cap suffices.
Concrete export timeout/byte/effort accounting and same-call cleanup/failed-command behavior require prospective tests. Export must consume frozen session budget/accounting symmetrically.
Actual full wrapper/source-owned tool build/setup can fail under fixed conditions; no prior green baseline or retry is invented.
Actual target Go effective context and package/file selection must match frozen source-expectation context; helper CGO0/GOWORKoff context is not the target context.
